scope: Independent source-only challenge of WPF/WinUI refund retry semantics against server refund handler, unique persistence index, and checked-in integration-test source. No tests executed; no source or registry changed.

assessment.confirmed_difference: WPF SubmitRefundAsync creates rreq-{Guid.NewGuid()} for each invocation, invokes RefundAsync once, and resets IsRefunding in finally. WPF ApiClient posts and parses HTTP results but has no transport-exception-to-OutcomeUnknown conversion. WinUI builds a request only when _pendingRefund is null; CompleteRefundAsync stores it before send, retains it for OutcomeUnknown, and reuses it on the next submit. It rotates the ID only after success. This is an in-memory recovery context; durability across process restart is not established by these files.
assessment.financial_effect_bound: A manual WPF re-submit after an ambiguous transport exception is a distinct idempotency command. If a prior partial refund committed, the second command may be another separately recorded refund, subject to the remaining-refund clamp and authorization. This is not evidence of an automatic retry, duplicate posting under one key, over-refund, or cash/account loss. Server locks the order and checks the protected source balance before recording the refund. A full already-refunded order has no positive remainder and is rejected.
assessment.server_and_test_counterevidence: Server derives refund-{RefundRequestId}, checks for a prior record, uses a locked order row, clamps to remaining refundable, protects the source account, and persists refund/movement within a transaction; the persistence model has a unique IdempotencyKey index. Checked-in tests cover sequential same-ID replay, concurrent same-ID single refund, and different-ID concurrent attempts capped at the order total. These are source observations only; tests were not run.
assessment.overlap_and_separation: This client recovery divergence is separate from FIN-CAND-REFUND-REPLAY-001. That candidate concerns same-key server replay behavior under overlapping full-refund requests: initial lookup precedes the order lock; if a sibling commits the full refund before the loser acquires the lock, the loser may observe zero remainder and fail before a unique-index conflict/replay path. The same-key concurrency test uses partial 8,000 refunds against a 20,000 order, so it does not establish the full-refund edge. Neither issue establishes duplicate financial movement. The WinUI pending request also remains process-local, so restart recovery is not proven.
assessment.deployment_and_policy: WPF source inclusion is confirmed; active deployment/support and desired behavior after an ambiguous refund are not established. No client deployment/config evidence was checked. Conditional low reliability/policy concern only; do not promote to a confirmed financial loss finding without deployment and workflow evidence.

source_references.evidence: Lines 81-90 create the request with a new rreq-Guid and send it. Lines 91-100 handle only returned ApiResult errors/success; lines 102-105 reset IsRefunding. No retained pending request/id is present in this method.

RefundAsync directly awaits PostAsJsonAsync and ReadResultAsync. ReadResultAsync maps HTTP statuses and catches malformed error-body parsing only. No transport exception mapping is shown on this command path.

Lines 84-85 prevent cancel/close while _pendingRefund exists. Lines 93-106 create only when no pending request, else reuse the same request. Lines 112-115 retain unresolved requests and clear after success or a non-unknown initial failure; line 117 rotates ID after success. No persistence mechanism is shown in this source span.
ReadAsync and SendAsync convert listed transport/serialization exceptions to OutcomeUnknown; SendAsync specifically tells the operator to retry the same data. RefundAsync routes through SendAsync.

Lines 47-50 derive and look up the request key before acquiring a transaction/order lock (56-63). Lines 78-83 clamp to refundable remainder; 91-93 check protected source balance; 102-106 construct the refund movement. Lines 108-135 apply/persist refund and movement and commit. Lines 137-150 roll back and retry lookup on constrained conflicts (with sibling wait for balance-lock contention). Lines 154-165 define replay lookup/result. The initial lookup is not repeated after obtaining the order lock before the business validation, leaving the noted same-key full-refund replay nuance distinct from duplicate posting.
The model declares a unique index over OrderRefund.IdempotencyKey.

Test source asserts sequential and concurrent same-key exactly-once behavior and different-key concurrent cumulative cap. The same-key concurrent scenario requests 8,000 against a 20,000 order; it does not test two overlapping full-refund requests.

untested_or_unverified: No tests executed; no runtime, SQL/provider, network-fault, or physical money workflow was exercised.
No test simulates WPF response loss after server commit followed by another manual submit.
No test verifies WinUI pending refund recovery after application restart or process termination.
No checked-in test in the cited range covers concurrent same-key requests whose amount fully consumes the order or an overlapping full-refund replay result.
WPF active deployment/support and the operator policy for ambiguous outcomes are unknown.
disposition: Corroborate the source-described client difference and conditional recovery concern. Keep severity conditional/low; do not classify as duplicate-payment/over-refund or merge with FIN-CAND-REFUND-REPLAY-001. The latter remains a separate server replay-result edge, not evidence of multiple movement postings.
